column30:
Thermal (heating and cooling) energy consumption in Ankara Metropolitan Municipality (AMM) reflects both the legacy of fossil-fuel dependency and the ongoing transition toward cleaner and more diversified sources. The largest share of heating demand is still met by natural gas, which supplies approximately 70% of total thermal consumption, in line with national and municipal data from the Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources (MENR), Turkish Statistical Institute (TURKSTAT), and ABB's Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP). Coal remains relevant in certain older district heating networks and in limited industrial facilities, accounting for about 10% of the thermal energy supply, while oil products (primarily heating oil) represent around 5%. These fossil sources together underline the city's continuing reliance on imported fuels and highlight the importance of accelerating the transition to domestic renewable solutions.

Renewable and alternative energy sources contribute around 15% of the thermal supply mix. Biomass and biofuels (5%) are utilized in small-scale heating applications, particularly in peri-urban and rural areas within municipal boundaries. Geothermal energy (6%) is increasingly significant due to regional resources, with district heating projects supplying residential and public facilities. Solar thermal energy (3%) is supported by government and municipal incentives, with rooftop and building-integrated solar collectors becoming more widespread. Waste-to-energy facilities contribute approximately 1% of thermal supply, while wastewater heat recovery (WWHR), though still in the pilot stage, accounts for a small but promising share of about 0.2%. In addition, a further 0.8% is attributed to other renewable sources, such as innovative pilot technologies currently under development. Nuclear and electricity-based heating are excluded from this section, as they are reported separately in the electricity consumption category.

This breakdown demonstrates that Ankara is gradually diversifying its heating and cooling mix, with renewables and innovative recovery solutions being prioritized under Local Climate Change Action Plan and SECAP commitments. AMM is actively implementing policies to increase the share of clean energy by promoting geothermal district heating, expanding solar collector deployment, and exploring further wastewater heat recovery potential.

column30: El cálculo del consumo total de energía térmica se hace a partir de estimaciones hechas en la EEL de Lo Barnechea, la cual estima que para el año 2022, el consumo térmico residencial fue de 11719 mWh y estima que el consumo residencial significó cerca del 50% del consumo de la comuna. A pesar de lo anterior, los datos obtenidos en esta categorías son insuficientes, ya que no existen estudios a nivel comunal de las fuentes de energía térmica. Por un lado, no existen datos del % del consumo eléctrico destinado a calefacción en la comuna. Por otro lado, las fuentes principales de energía para calefacción son gas natural licuado vendido a granel o en red. Si bien existen 4 empresas en la comuna que abastecen de gas natural licuado, sólo se obtuvieron datos de una de estas empresas. Se está trabajando en obtener datos de las otras 3 empresas para tener un cálculo más preciso, sin embargo, hasta el momento no existe información precisa sobre el % de consumo de energía para calefacción de fuentes eléctricas.
